item.dc:creator: Jennifer Camp Forbes
item.dc:description: <p>Jennifer Camp Forbes is currently a senior shopping editor at Who What Wear, where she has worked in a variety of capacities for over a decade, including creative director and various editor roles. She’s well-known as a shopping expert that’s sought out for advice and insight on the latest trends, outfit ideas, and fashion picks thanks to her thoughtful shopping roundups, digital moodboards, and extensive knowledge of up-and-coming brands, plus the new arrivals sections of the chicest retailers. Jennifer has had a lifelong interest in fashion which led her to intern at Harper’s Bazaar as an undergraduate. Later, while working towards her masters degree in psychological counseling at Columbia University, she founded two digital fashion publications: Le Fashion and Olsens Anonymous. The popularity of both sites grew and after graduation she decided put her plans to become a therapist aside to pursue a career in fashion. While she has called Los Angeles and New York City home in the past, she currently works remotely from Massachusetts. When she’s not obsessing over and writing about her latest fashion finds, she is delighting in raising two little ones with her highschool sweetheart, perusing TikTok religiously, listening to podcasts and audiobooks, creating abstract photographs, and eating the best Mexican food she can get her hands on.</p>

item.title: From Perfume to Sweaters: These Are the Nordstrom Black Friday Deals That Matter
item.dc:content:
Although Black Friday isn't technically until tomorrow, the sales start earlier and earlier each year, and many of the discounts have already been going on for days across brands and retailers. At Nordstrom, there's up to 60% off, and our editors have been covering the sale from all angles. Yesterday, I covered the discounted jeans, coats, and sweaters. Jennifer Camp Forbes shared the top trends that are marked down (fur-trimmed coats and jackets, ballet pumps, relaxed jeans, cropped trench coats, and woven bags), and Chichi Offer covered the sneaker discounts.

Today, I focused on beauty, fashion, and home items. For beauty, Dyson blow dryers are one of the most purchases every year. Another top contender is the TheraFace Mask Glo LED Skincare Mask. In the clothing section, two staples that I noticed immediately are the 501 '90s jeans, which are a best seller, and Leset's cropped flare pants. Editorial director Lauren Eggertsen has the taffeta Olina pants from Reformation, which is one of the biggest pant trends of the year. For home recommendations, Flamingo Estate makes the best candles. Other highlights include brands like Le Creuset, Moccamaster, KitchenAid, and Shark.

item.title: I Fear Zara’s Black Friday Sale Is My Entire Personality—8 Items I Added Straight to Basket
item.dc:content:
If there's one 2026 Black Friday sale I'll always pay attention to, it's Zara's. The brand has become rather good at making the kind of pieces I would normally reserve for a more expensive shopping list—great coats, leather accessories, suede shoes, party-season dresses—feel considerably more attainable, and Black Friday is usually when I'll have a particularly close look.

The good news? Zara's 2026 Black Friday sale has now begun! It officially started on Thursday, 26 November at 8 pm online and in store, ahead of Black Friday itself on Friday, 27 November. Interestingly, Zara had already added what the discount would be across items in the sale ahead of the prices actually dropping at 8 pm. I like this—there are no surprises, no lingering in the hope that the piece you have your eye on will be discounted—it's all there right now in black and white (and red). As with previous years, the brand is offering up to 40% off selected pieces, rather than applying one blanket discount across everything.

And this is where I think Zara's Black Friday sale is actually worth paying attention to. I'm not particularly interested in buying something purely because it's 40% off; if I didn't want it yesterday, I probably don't need it today. Instead, I tend to use Black Friday as an excuse to revisit the pieces that have been sitting in my shopping basket or saved items for a while—particularly the things with a slightly heftier price tag. Think a really good coat that you'll wear every winter, a pair of leather boots that can anchor half your wardrobe, a suede jacket, a beautifully cut blazer, a cashmere jumper or a leather bag. Those are the purchases where a decent discount can make a meaningful difference, rather than simply giving you an excuse to buy three more things you don't need.

Now that Zara's 2026 Black Friday sale is underway, I've rounded up my edit of the chicest pieces, plus everything you need to know about the 2026 sale below. Because if you're going to partake in Black Friday, it definitely pays to have a plan.

Zara Black Friday 2026 Sale FAQs

When is the Zara Black Friday sale 2026?

Zara's Black Friday 2026 sale is live now! The sale started at 8 pm on Thursday 26 November 2026, the evening before Black Friday. The sale is live in-store and online.

How Much Will Zara's Black Friday 2026 Sale Discount Be?

Zara has confirmed the discount for its 2026 Black Friday sale and, like previous years, is offering up to 40% off selected items.

Does Zara do Black Friday?

Yes. Zara has offered Black Friday discounts in recent years, usually on selected products rather than across the entire site. The brand tends to keep its promotion relatively understated, which means the pieces worth buying can disappear quickly once the sale begins.

When Does Zara's Black Friday 2026 Sale End?

Zara has not yet confirmed when its 2026 Black Friday sale will end. Black Friday falls on Friday 27 November, followed by Cyber Monday on Monday 30 November, so we'd expect the sale period to run across the weekend, although the exact dates and timings will depend on Zara's final announcement.

What Should I Buy From Zara in the 2026 Black Friday Sale?

My advice? Don't start with the discount. Start with the wardrobe gap. I'm much more likely to use Zara's Black Friday sale to buy a coat, leather boots, a suede piece or a really good bag than I am to stock up on £20 tops simply because they're reduced. The best Black Friday purchases are the things you'd genuinely have considered buying at full price and that you'll still be excited to wear six months from now.

Black Friday 2026 FAQs

What Is Black Friday?

Black Friday is an annual shopping event when brands and retailers offer discounts across fashion, beauty, homeware, technology and more. Originating in the United States, it takes place the day after Thanksgiving and has become one of the biggest shopping events of the year in the UK. Today, Black Friday sales often begin weeks before the official date, giving shoppers the opportunity to find deals on everything from wardrobe staples to Christmas gifts.

When Is Black Friday 2026?

Black Friday 2026 falls on Friday, 27 November. However, many brands launch their Black Friday sales in the weeks leading up to the date, with some offers available throughout November. The Black Friday shopping period typically continues over the weekend and into Cyber Monday on Monday, 30 November.

When do Black Friday Sales Start in 2026?

Black Friday sales in 2026 are expected to begin at different times depending on the brand or retailer. Whilst Black Friday itself takes place on Friday, 27 November, many brands launch early offers in the weeks beforehand. Check back regularly for the latest Black Friday deals from your favourite fashion and beauty retailers.

When Do Black Friday Sales End in 2026?

There is no official end date for Black Friday sales. Many retailers extend their offers throughout the Black Friday weekend and into Cyber Monday on Monday, 30 November 2026, whilst others may end their promotions earlier or continue discounting into December. Always check individual retailers for confirmed sale dates and terms.

Which Brands Are Taking Part in Black Friday 2026?

From designer handbags to jewellery and beauty favourites, plenty of brands are offering discounts for Black Friday 2026. This year, you can shop deals from brands including Zara, DeMellier, Missoma, Dyson and Elemis, with offers across selected styles and collections. We might even have a few exclusive discounts up our sleeves for you, too! We've rounded up the sales worth knowing about to help you find the best fashion and beauty deals.

What Should I Buy During the Black Friday Sales?

Black Friday is a good opportunity to invest in fashion and beauty pieces you've had your eye on, replenish everyday essentials or get ahead with Christmas shopping. Look out for discounts on winter coats, boots, cashmere, bags, skincare, makeup and fragrance. Before buying, compare prices and check the terms of each offer to make sure you're getting a worthwhile deal.

Are Black Friday Deals Worth It?

Black Friday can be a useful time to shop for fashion and beauty at reduced prices, but not every offer represents the best value. If there's a particular item you've been considering, check its price before the sale begins and compare offers across retailers. Shopping with a wish list in mind can also help you prioritise pieces you'll genuinely wear or use. Our recommendations are selected by our editors who weigh up all the options for you, so you can trust their selections are, in their opinion, worth it.

Where Can I Find the Best Black Friday Fashion and Beauty Deals?

For the best Black Friday fashion and beauty deals, start with the brands and retailers you already love, then compare prices across different stockists. Who What Wear UK will be rounding up standout discounts, editor-approved buys and the fashion and beauty pieces worth shopping. Check our latest Black Friday coverage for updates on the best deals.

When Is Black Friday 2027?

Black Friday 2027 falls on Friday, 26 November. The annual shopping event takes place on the Friday after U.S. Thanksgiving, so its date changes each year. Many retailers are likely to launch deals ahead of the official date, with Cyber Monday following on Monday, 29 November 2027.

item.dc:creator: Maxine Eggenberger
item.dc:description: <p>Maxine Eggenberger is Who What Wear UK’s deputy editor and has over fourteen years of experience in fashion journalism. She been creating engaging and elevated style content specifically for Who What Wear UK since 2018, covering runway reports, emerging trends, long-form features, self-styled shopping stories and columns, including her edit of the <a href="https://www.whowhatwear.co.uk/maxine-eggenberger-shopping-picks"><u>best new-in buys</u></a>. She ensures the highest editorial standards are met across the site, leads the editorial team in their SEO strategy and keyword planning, works closely with the beauty team on content initiatives, represents the brand at industry events, and regularly contributes to social media, including her own Who What Wear UK <a href="https://www.tiktok.com/@whowhatwear.uk?lang=en"><u>TikTok</u></a> franchise, French Style Fridays. Previously, Maxine appeared on ITV's <em>This Morning</em> in her own fashion segment and has interviewed countless celebrities—everyone from Victoria Beckham to Oscar winner Lupita Nyong’o.</p><p>Prior to Who What Wear UK, Maxine’s career began when, after completing her first-ever internship at Look magazine, she was offered a position on the brand's fashion desk. She accepted, leaving university a year early in the process. Her passion and natural talent for writing and styling meant she swiftly rose through the ranks to become the title's fashion news and commercial content editor, with a stint as InStyle.co.uk’s fashion and beauty writer along the way. She later served as Look’s acting Editor in Chief, overseeing both print and digital, before embarking on a successful freelance career, working with Grazia, The Pool, and Marie Claire amongst others. </p><p>Maxine is based remotely from her countryside home near Edinburgh where she spends her downtime renovating her house, walking her dogs, hosting friends and trying to master the art of making Old Fashioned cocktails. </p>

item.title: Aestheticians Tell Me This On-Sale Brand is the Secret to Your Clearest, Glowiest Skin Yet
item.dc:content:
While I can be picky about my winter skincare products, there's one brand I always feel confident reaching for when the air turns cold and dry in California. Many aestheticians have recommended its products to me over the years and they've never steered me wrong. In fact, Sloan Studios founder Malika Sloan says it's the secret to both her clients' and her own glowing complexion. "I've been working with PCA Skin for nearly a decade, and it’s a brand I genuinely love and trust both professionally and personally," she says.

She also confesses that the brand's chemical peels have been a staple in her treatment room for years. "Whether I'm treating acne, aging, hyperpigmentation, scarring, or enlarged pores, I can always find a peel or treatment protocol that addresses my client's specific concerns," she adds. I'm honestly obsessed with the brand and think their at-home products are just as worth investing in!"

If that vote of confidence wasn't enough for you, more to come. There are so many aestheticians and editors who believe in the brand. I've been hooked on it myself for years and had to share some exciting news about it. PCA Skin is currently offering 20% off sitewide for Black Friday through November 30. Snag the below aesthetician- and editor-favorites while you can at a discount—I know I'll be stocking up.
PCA Skin
ReBalance Cream

Choosing a daily moisturizer can be tough. For me, it needs to do a few things at once: hydrate my skin properly and keep it hydrated for longer periods of time, all while delivering a healthy glow. I've found that some moisturizers provide the right hydration, but leave me looking kind of dull. Sloan just gave me her top recommendation for the perfect do-it-all moisturizer that's 20% off for Black Friday.

"This is probably one of my personal favorites! I love how incredibly lightweight it is. It absorbs beautifully into the skin but still leaves behind the prettiest, healthy-looking glow. It's especially great for anyone who wants hydration without a heavy or greasy feel. I also love recommending it to acne-prone clients because it provides moisture without feeling occlusive. It's easy to layer and build into virtually any skin care routine." — Sloan
PCA Skin
Daily Cleansing Oil

Aestheticians always cite this cleansing oil as one of their most used and loved products from PCA Skin. I was introduced to this silky, makeup-busting formula by master aesthetician Caroline Crosskill. It's so lightweight and hydrating without leaving a greasy film. It also never clogs my pores and easily removes even full coverage foundation and mascara.

Sloan also loves this formula. "This is one of my favorite first steps in a nighttime cleansing routine, especially for anyone who wears makeup or SPF daily," she says. "I love using it as a pre-cleanse to break down makeup, sunscreen, and excess oil without disrupting the skin's natural moisture barrier. It's a great way to thoroughly cleanse the skin while keeping it feeling soft and nourished."
PCA Skin
Hyaluronic Acid Boosting Serum

If there were ever a perfect serum for dry or dehydrated winter skin, it would be this one. This silky hyaluronic acid serum is a favorite of team Who What Wear, but you can also rest easy knowing it's backed by the professionals. There's also a clear reason why it remains a constant best seller for the brand.

"This is the hydration that actually lasts," says celebrity aesthetician Candice Miele, who's behind the glow of stars like Kendall Jenner, Gabrielle Union, and Hailey Bieber . "It's not just hyaluronic acid sitting on top of your skin—it works on three levels: surface hydration, deeper hydration, and it helps your skin make more of its own hyaluronic acid. That's why I love it. It plumps fine lines, it smooths, and it strengthens your barrier with ceramides and niacinamide at the same time. If your skin feels tight, dull, or just dehydrated no matter what moisturizer you use, start here. Morning and night, on damp skin."
PCA Skin
Hydrating Toner

This TikTok viral toner is a personal favorite of mine. It gently exfoliates, but adds an extra dose of hydration without leaving me feeling greasy. Over time, it also gives you this lit-from-within glow when combined with the Hyaluronic Acid Boosting Serum.
PCA Skin
Pore Refining Treatment

"This is the one I call my reset. It consists of three kinds of exfoliation in one: physical from rice powder and pumice, enzymatic from papaya, and [chemical] from mandelic acid. Plus, the clays—kaolin and bentonite—pull oil and gunk out of the pores. So, you get smoother texture, smaller-looking pores, and that clean, polished glow without stripping your skin. Use it one to three times a week, not every day. Perfect if you're congested, rough, or your makeup isn't sitting right." — Miele

PCA Skin
Vitamin B3 Serum

For any other sensitive folks out there who can't handle vitamin C, aestheticians love this pick as an alternative. I haven't tried this one myself just yet, but best believe I'll be taking advantage of the sale to do so.

“This is my brightening pick, especially if vitamin C stings or you experience sensitivity with it. It's 6% niacinamide, so it helps fade dark spots, even out tone, calm redness, and strengthen your barrier. It also helps with that dull, yellowish look skin gets with age. I love it because it does a lot without irritating—brightening, calming, and barrier support in one step. If you have dark spots, redness, or uneven tone, this is your serum." — Miele
PCA Skin
Nutrient Toner

Honestly, this toner is a fall season dream, containing pumpkin wine, vitamins, amino acids, and enzymes to gently exfoliate the skin. Sloan, whose skin speaks for itself, is a huge fan. "I'm obsessed with this toner," she says. "First of all, it smells like a pumpkin spice latte, which makes it such a treat to use. But beyond the scent, it contains gentle exfoliating ingredients that help improve skin texture and promote a healthy glow without leaving the skin feeling stripped or tight. I love that it's gentle enough for a variety of skin types and is a great way to incorporate mild exfoliation into your everyday routine."
PCA Skin
Weightless Protection Broad Spectrum SPF 45

Finding the right sunscreen can be tricky, especially if you have a darker skin tone and are looking to forego the dreaded whitecast. This formula, though, is one of my top picks. It's hydrating and lightweight on the skin and, it's an elegant chemical formula that doesn't leave a cast on the skin.

Miele feels the same way about this formula. "This is non-negotiable," she shares. "No serum matters if you're not protecting your skin. I love this one because it actually disappears. No white cast, no grease, no heavy feeling—which is why people will actually wear it every day. It's SPF 45, broad spectrum, made for normal, combination, oily and acne-prone skin, and it has caffeine and antioxidants for extra defense against free radicals. Put it on last every morning. Every day."
PCA Skin
Detoxifying Mask

"Think of this as your weekly at-home skin reset! I especially love this mask for clients with oily or congested skin. It helps draw out impurities, absorb excess oil, and leave the skin feeling refreshed and clarified. I love recommending a weekly mask as a way to supplement professional treatments and maintain results between appointments. It's a great addition for anyone who feels like their skin needs a little extra TLC." — Sloan
PCASkin
Hyaluronic Acid Lip Booster

If your lips are perpetually dry and cracked during the winter like mine, this lip treatment is one of the best I've ever used to quell any dryness. Sloan is also a fan. "This is such a great addition to any skincare routine, especially for anyone focused on hydration and maintaining a smooth, healthy-looking lip," she says. "I love peptide-based products because they're a great way to incorporate skin-supporting ingredients beyond just your face. It's one of those products that feels like a little luxury but is also incredibly practical for everyday use."
PCA Skin
Collagen Hydrator

While Sloan called out the ReBalance Cream as a solid glow-inducing option, I have to add to that and share my personal favorite PCA Skin moisturizer. This rich moisturizer plumps, hydrates, and gives my skin a glassy sheen like no other. It also is one of the best moisturizers that gets me through the dry winter months in Los Angeles.

While I can be picky about my winter skincare products, there's one brand I always feel confident reaching for when the air turns cold and dry in California. Many aestheticians have recommended its products to me over the years and they've never steered me wrong. In fact, Sloan Studios founder Malika Sloan says it's the secret to both her clients' and her own glowing complexion. "I've been working with PCA Skin for nearly a decade, and it’s a brand I genuinely love and trust both professionally and personally," she says.

She also confesses that the brand's chemical peels have been a staple in her treatment room for years. "Whether I'm treating acne, aging, hyperpigmentation, scarring, or enlarged pores, I can always find a peel or treatment protocol that addresses my client's specific concerns," she adds. I'm honestly obsessed with the brand and think their at-home products are just as worth investing in!"

If that vote of confidence wasn't enough for you, more to come. There are so many aestheticians and editors who believe in the brand. I've been hooked on it myself for years and had to share some exciting news about it. PCA Skin is currently offering 20% off sitewide for Black Friday through November 30. Snag the below aesthetician- and editor-favorites while you can at a discount—I know I'll be stocking up.
PCA Skin
ReBalance Cream

Choosing a daily moisturizer can be tough. For me, it needs to do a few things at once: hydrate my skin properly and keep it hydrated for longer periods of time, all while delivering a healthy glow. I've found that some moisturizers provide the right hydration, but leave me looking kind of dull. Sloan just gave me her top recommendation for the perfect do-it-all moisturizer that's 20% off for Black Friday.

"This is probably one of my personal favorites! I love how incredibly lightweight it is. It absorbs beautifully into the skin but still leaves behind the prettiest, healthy-looking glow. It's especially great for anyone who wants hydration without a heavy or greasy feel. I also love recommending it to acne-prone clients because it provides moisture without feeling occlusive. It's easy to layer and build into virtually any skin care routine." — Sloan
PCA Skin
Daily Cleansing Oil

Aestheticians always cite this cleansing oil as one of their most used and loved products from PCA Skin. Hyaluronic Acid Boosting Serum

There's also a clear reason why it remains a constant best seller for the brand.

"This is the hydration that actually lasts," says celebrity aesthetician Candice Miele, who's behind the glow of stars like Kendall Jenner, Gabrielle Union, and Hailey Bieber . If your skin feels tight, dull, or just dehydrated no matter what moisturizer you use, start here. Morning and night, on damp skin."
PCA Skin
Hydrating Toner

PCA Skin
Pore Refining Treatment

item.title: Londoners Don't Do "Boring"—5 Elegant Winter Shoe Trends Worth Copying From the Capital
item.dc:content:
I was sat on the Tube the other day, shaking the rain off my umbrella, when I realised: if there's anything that Londoners know how to do well, it's making winter dressing look effortlessly cool. It makes sense, after all; British weather is mostly rain and grey skies (so we've got plenty of experience with dressing practically), but there's something in the way London women make a coat and jeans feel stylish that I think comes down to their shoes.

Footwear always does a lot of the heavy lifting. From the fashion crowds of Soho to the painfully cool dressers of East London, a good pair of shoes is sure to go the distance (pun very much intended), and winter 2026 is bringing a fresh batch of shoe trends into the spotlight. Think sleek knee-high boots, smart loafers and '90s sock boots that add just the right amount of interest to an otherwise understated outfit. This season is a little playful, a little dressy, but always comfortable, so you're covered for just about every occasion.

And the best part? These aren't trends that require a complete wardrobe overhaul (no runway-ready stilettos in sight), just the shoes that the Big Smoke's best dressed are really investing in now for everyday wear. So, whether you're looking to update your capsule wardrobe or to simply find a pair that makes your favourite cold-weather outfit feel new again, these are the winter shoe trends worth knowing this season.

5 London Winter Shoe Trends for 2026

1. Sock Boots

Style Notes: Sleek, streamlined and always chic, sock boots are making a welcome return to the winter footwear conversation in 2026. After several seasons dominated by chunky, chained-up bikers, the fashion set is embracing something new in the second-skin silhouette, and it has our full attention. Spotted across the autumn/winter 2026 runways and championed by minimalist brands like The Row, Toteme and Dear Frances, this season's iterations feel more grown-up than their noughties predecessors.

Think supple leather, stretchy finishes, pointed toes and unexpected flat soles, with styles ranging from barely-there ankle boots to knee-high designs that fit like a glove. The beauty of the trend lies in its versatility, too. Wear yours with jeans and an evening coat à la Rikke (pictured above) for a high-low look that feels effortlessly polished.

Shop Sock Boots:
Dear Frances
Balla Bootie

One of the OG sock boot styles.

Charles & Keith
Faux Suede Stitch-Trim Heeled Ankle Boots

I love this buttercream colourway.

Jonak
Thigh-High Boots in Black Stretch

Yes, you can wear sock boots as thigh-highs too.

Whistles
Chocolate Hera Stretch Suede Boot

How about a suede pair for all your dinner plans?

The Row
Cindy Stretch Boot

Just add an oversized cream knit and slightly cropped trousers.

2. Knee-High Flat Boots

Style Notes: Practicality and polish come together in one of this season's most wearable footwear trends: the flat knee-high boot. Finally, those who love the aesthetic of a tall boot don't have to succumb to skinny stiletto heels; no, this is a firm favourite amongst London's fashion set who spend more time on-the-go than limping around dancefloors. Whether you prefer understated suede or equestrian-inspired details, rich chocolate-brown and classic black styles are leading the charge, offering an alternative to summer's more statement-making sandals and autumn's chunky boots (but more on those later).

Better still, they're incredibly easy to style, so wear yours with your favourite knit, mini skirt and an oversized coat for an off-duty look comfortable enough for a day spent navigating the city, but chic enough to take you straight from the office to dinner too.

Shop Knee-High Flat Boots:
Khaite
Colt Leather Knee-High Boots

Okay, forget a wish list—these are all I want this Christmas.

Dune London
Tallo Boot in Brown

Perfect for tucking leggings into.

M&S
Buckle Riding Round Toe Knee High Boot

Buckle up! Riding boots are tapping into the Western trend that's picking up traction for spring/summer 2027.

Coach
Riding Boot

Pure elegance.

The White Company
Chunky Tall Riding Boot

Just add a boxy blazer, leggings and a cap for a rich-looking weekend 'fit.

3. Grandad Loafers

Style Notes: If it looks like it would pair perfectly with a big cardigan and a pipe, I'm inclined to say it may actually be chic. The "grandad loafer" is giving classic preppy footwear a cool-girl update this winter, and Londoners are comfortably on board. Tapping into the wider vintage-meets-country aesthetic, this season is all about embracing traditional, menswear-inspired styles in worn-in suede and brown leather styled up with a contemporary twist.

Whilst mock-croc, patent and slipper-style shoes are on the rise for spring, right now you'll see plenty of slouchy, tailored trousers, baggy jeans or ladylike midi skirts worn with white socks and "grandad loafers", conclusive proof that sometimes the best wardrobe additions are the ones that have been around for decades.

Shop Grandad Loafers:

Boden
Super Soft Flexi Loafer-Bitter Chocolate

I've never regretted a pair of Boden shoes.

ALOHAS
Aven Rift Burgundy Leather Loafers

Alohas are known for its loafers, and it's easy to see why.

Saint Laurent
Le Loafer Supple in Suede

Get them now before they sell out.
COS
Split Suede Mocassin Loafers

Just a slight heel for a little extra lift.

H&M
Loafers

These are from H&M's Premium Selection, so care has gone into the fabrication and construction.

4. Techy Trainers

Style Notes: Londoners and trainers go together like winter and flu season, so you're unlikely to spot one without the other. We might have flirted with satin ballet styles, luxe suede and clean white kicks, but in a post-Salomon era we're still invested in gorpcore, techy trainers with all of the bells and whistles (even if there isn't any treacherous terrain in Belgravia).

Sporty, streamlined silhouettes are winning favour over bulkier, wide fits, but especially in a "go outdoors" colour palette of earthy browns, grounding black and pops of energising metallics. If you really want to style them like a Londoner, forget rustly windbreakers and stack up cosy layers of chunky knits, corduroy and cashmere scarves.

Shop Techy Trainers:
New Balance
1890A Leather-Trimmed Mesh Sneakers

There's something Y2K party about this New Balance style.

Keen
Jasper Trainers

ICYMI, Keen trainers are the latest hot topic.

Salomon
XT-Whisper Gore-Tex

Just add a faux-fur coat, grey jumper and baggy blue jeans.

NIKE
Shox Z Premium Patent-Leather Trimmed Shell Sneakers

Black goes with everything.

New Balance
Tl900 Sneaker

You can't tell me that these don't look incredibly comfortable.

5. Lug-Sole Boots

Style Notes: For those who are looking for something a little more hardy, the heavy-duty lug sole hasn't gone away; it's simply been reinvented. If jeans tucked into moto boots wasn't exactly your vibe, don't worry—you'll spot some of the capital's best dressed wearing their big boots underneath their jeans and long trousers, with just the toes poking out. More recently, snow-proof boots are feeling more pared-back and polished and are worn mostly for their shape and height, so if sock boots felt a bridge too far, you know where you're at with a stacked style that's sure to brave the weather.

Shop Lug-Sole Boots:

Kurt Geiger
Kingly Biker

I can't stop thinking about the myriad ways I would wear these.

ME+EM
Zip Front Boot

The glossy leather adds such a premium finish.

Jimmy Choo
Biker Rain

Jimmy Choo is an expert in sought-after styles.

Steve Madden
Jones Dark Brown Suede

How to get The Row on a much smaller budget.
item.dc:creator: Remy Farrell
item.dc:description: <p>Remy Farrell is a London-based shopping editor with nearly 10 years of editorial experience covering fashion, beauty and lifestyle. After graduating with a journalism degree and working on the editorial and fashion teams for titles such as Grazia, Elle, Cosmopolitan and British Vogue, she moved into the luxury e-commerce sector, working as fashion assistant at <a href="http://outnet.com/">TheOutnet.com</a>, styling for the social media channels and helping to develop the collections for the in-house brand Iris & Ink. After expanding an assisting and styling portfolio that includes shooting talent such as Gigi Hadid, Victoria Beckham and Miquita Oliver, she also branched out into beauty, following a lifelong passion for the field, creating tried-and-tested reviews and diverse beauty content. </p><p>In her newly appointed role as Fashion Editor at Who What Wear starting in 2024, Remy is interested in discovering new and exciting fashion and beauty brands to share with the Who What Wear readership. Although she has luxury experience, her main focus is uncovering hidden gems at affordable prices to make shopping accessible to everyone, no matter their budget. In her spare time you can find her reading, attending boxing classes, but most likely, shopping. </p>

item.title: I Have Sensitive Eyes—I Thought Eye Cream Was Off-Limits Until I Tried These Derm-Recommended Formulas
item.dc:content:
I've recently become an eye cream convert. For years, I was sceptical of these miniature pots and tubes; they contain many of the same ingredients as our face creams and are often more expensive to boot. But after much testing, I've really come around to their merits, especially as I have sensitive eyes. The skin in this area is already much thinner and more delicate than the rest of our face, meaning it's generally more reactive too. In fact, experts agree: you can really benefit from a dedicated formula that's less likely to cause irritation.

As consultant dermatologist Dr Zainab Laftah tells me, the skin around the eyes is so thin that it's actually more prone to sensitivity and irritation than the rest of your face. Not to mention, face creams are usually too heavy or contain too many actives for this area. She continues, "Signs and symptoms of sensitive skin around the eyes include redness, itching, dryness, flaking, stinging or burning, particularly after applying skincare or makeup products."

If you've ever experienced these reactions, it doesn't mean you need to stop applying eye cream; you just need to find the right one for your particular needs.

What Eye Creams Are Suitable for Sensitive Skin?

There is an array of eye creams that work for sensitive skin, but ensure you pay close attention to the packaging. "Look for gentle, hydrating ingredients such as glycerin and hyaluronic acid, which help attract and retain moisture, and ceramides, which support the skin’s natural protective barrier," says Dr Laftah. "Choose fragrance-free formulations specifically suitable for use around the eyes, as even soothing ingredients can occasionally cause irritation."

What Ingredients to Avoid

As expected, those with sensitive skin, especially around the eyes, should steer clear of strong active ingredients such as retinols, exfoliating acids like glycolic acid (AHAs) and salicylic acid (BHAs), as well as high-strength vitamin C, as these can cause dryness, stinging and irritation, notes Dr Laftah.

Can Sensitive Skin Types Use Actives Around the Eyes?

"Yes," says Dr Laftah, "But it is important to choose gentle, well-formulated products specifically designed for this delicate area. Ingredients such as low-strength retinol or vitamin C may be tolerated by some individuals, but should be introduced gradually to minimise the risk of dryness, redness and irritation." As always, avoid applying actives to already irritated or inflamed skin, and discontinue use if persistent irritation occurs.

Without further ado, shop some of my and Dr Laftah's favourite eye creams for sensitive eyes.

The Best Eye Creams for Sensitive Eyes

  • Best Overall Eye Cream: Bioderma Atoderm Intensive Eye Cream, £18
  • Best for Allergy-Prone Skin: La Roche-Posay Toleriane Dermallergo Eye Cream, £25
  • Best for Dry Skin: Kiehl's Creamy Eye Treatment with Avocado, £50
  • Best Budget Eye Cream: Byoma Barrier Repair Eye Cream, £14
  • Best Luxury Eye Cream: Tatcha The Silk Peony Line-Smoothing Eye Cream, £72
  • Best Eye Cream With Actives: Medik8 Crystal Retinal Ceramide Eye, £42

1. Bioderma Atoderm Intensive Eye Cream

Best overall

Bioderma
Atoderm Intensive 3-In-1 Eye Care

Pros

  • Gentle enough for the whole family
  • Multiple-use formula targets dryness and provides ample hydration
  • Excellent price point
  • fragrance-free, ophthalmologically tested, and suitable for contact lens wearers

Cons

  • May not be plumping enough for those concerned about fine lines and wrinkles
  • Contains no active ingredients to target pigmentation or dark circles

Why we love it: If you want something ultra-soothing and gentle, Bioderma's eye cream is even safe for newborns. This is a fantastic all-rounder for anyone with very sensitive, dry or eczema-prone skin around the eyes. It's a three-in-one formula that not only hydrates, but also soothes irritation and helps repair the skin barrier.

I was particularly impressed by its patented ingredients, which include a complex that helps limit the adhesion of bacteria that can aggravate dryness. It also contains hyaluronic acid to maintain hydration and plumpness for up to 24 hours. Crucially, it's fragrance-free, ophthalmologically tested, and suitable for contact lens wearers—in fact, it's so gentle it's safe for babies from birth. This is not the product if you're looking for active ingredients, but if you want something gentle, soothing and hydrating, this is it.

2. La Roche-Posay Toleriane Dermallergo Eye Cream

Best for allergy-prone skin
La Roche-Posay
Toleriane Dermallergo Eye Cream

Pros

  • A standout for allergy sufferers and eczema-prone eyes
  • Fragrance free
  • Very gentle and good for day and night
  • Great price point

Cons

  • Small volume of product in tube

Why we love it: This soothing formula won't irritate even allergy-prone skin. If you have allergy-prone eyes, or are susceptible to redness and watering, La Roche-Posay's Toleriane Dermallergo Eye Cream is a true hero product. This soothing, lightweight fluid is approved by Allergy UK (and works particularly well for eczema-prone eyes, too)—but its targeted ingredients do more than simply soothe. There's the brand's thermal spring water to help calm discomfort, moisture-locking squalane, and niacinamide to hydrate and strengthen the skin barrier. It's certainly one for hay fever season, but it's an excellent everyday eye cream in its own right, too.

3. Kiehl's Creamy Eye Treatment with Avocado

Pros

  • Deeply hydrating, creamy formula with a blend of oils
  • Squalene for long-lasting nourishment

  • Does little to brighten under eyes or tackle pigmentation
  • On the pricier end
  • Pot packaging is less hygienic than a tube

Why we love it: This creamy formula is packed with multiple hydrators for long-lasting moisture. Sensitive skin tends to be some of the driest, and even gentle formulas can fall short when it comes to packing a moisture punch. That's why, especially during these chilly months, I've returned to an old stalwart: Kiehl's Creamy Eye Treatment With Avocado. I've been using it on and off for the past decade, but I love that the latest formula includes 75% more avocado oil than the previous version. Then there's also squalene and shea butter to deeply re-nourish depleted eye contours, and caffeine to combat tiredness and puffiness.

4. Byoma Barrier Repair Eye Cream

Barrier Repair Eye Cream

Pros

  • Powerful blend of active ingredients, including lipids, copper tripeptides and ectoin

  • Good price point
  • Dermatologist tested

  • Lacking targeted ingredients for those concerned with pigmentation, puffiness or dark circles
  • Pot packaging increases risk of bacteria

It's packed with ceramides and free from potential irritants, making it a great option for even the most sensitive eyes. It keeps things simple, which is often exactly what you need. The lightweight texture also absorbs quickly and sits nicely under makeup.

9. Roc Retinol Correxion Anti Ageing Wrinkle Eye Cream

Best targeted treatment

RoC
Retinol Correxion Line Smoothing Eye Cream

Pros

  • Balanced dose of nourishing and active ingredients
  • Stabilised dose of retinol at a very low percentage
  • No added fragrance or alcohol
  • Excellent price point and ergonomic applicator

Cons

  • Can get through product quickly if using night and day

Why we love it: A stabilised dose of retinol and barrier-supporting ingredients make this a great introduction to the active. As Dr Laftah mentions, sensitive eye types do not need to steer clear of actives entirely; they just need to ensure they introduce them slowly and in small increments.

There's a stabilised dose of retinol, formulated for the thin under-eye area, and there are also no added fragrances or drying alcohols. I've personally had no adverse side effects from this, but as always, patch test first.

How I Tested

Both the wider Who What Wear UK team and our beauty team have tested hundreds of eye creams between us. From more affordable products to luxury brands, we tested the gamut of price points and rated each one on how gentle it was on sensitive skin types, as well as tackling broader under-eye concerns, like puffiness, firmness and reducing hyperpigmentation.

Why Trust Us

At Who What Wear UK, we know that beauty isn’t one-size-fits-all. Our editors have tested thousands of products, including skincare, makeup, hair and nails, over the years and work closely with trusted experts—dermatologists, make-up artists and leading industry insiders—to ensure every guide is well-researched, inclusive and relevant to you.

We focus on formulas that deliver, whether they’re affordable favourites or luxury investments. Our product selection is based on tangible results, ingredient know-how and what we’d truly recommend to a friend.

I've recently become an eye cream convert. For years, I was sceptical of these miniature pots and tubes; they contain many of the same ingredients as our face creams and are often more expensive to boot. But after much testing, I've really come around to their merits, especially as I have sensitive eyes. The skin in this area is already much thinner and more delicate than the rest of our face, meaning it's generally more reactive too. In fact, experts agree: you can really benefit from a dedicated formula that's less likely to cause irritation.

As consultant dermatologist Dr Zainab Laftah tells me, the skin around the eyes is so thin that it's actually more prone to sensitivity and irritation than the rest of your face. Not to mention, face creams are usually too heavy or contain too many actives for this area. She continues, "Signs and symptoms of sensitive skin around the eyes include redness, itching, dryness, flaking, stinging or burning, particularly after applying skincare or makeup products."

If you've ever experienced these reactions, it doesn't mean you need to stop applying eye cream; you just need to find the right one for your particular needs.

What Eye Creams Are Suitable for Sensitive Skin?

There is an array of eye creams that work for sensitive skin, but ensure you pay close attention to the packaging. "Look for gentle, hydrating ingredients such as glycerin and hyaluronic acid, which help attract and retain moisture, and ceramides, which support the skin’s natural protective barrier," says Dr Laftah. "Choose fragrance-free formulations specifically suitable for use around the eyes, as even soothing ingredients can occasionally cause irritation."

What Ingredients to Avoid

As expected, those with sensitive skin, especially around the eyes, should steer clear of strong active ingredients such as retinols, exfoliating acids like glycolic acid (AHAs) and salicylic acid (BHAs), as well as high-strength vitamin C, as these can cause dryness, stinging and irritation, notes Dr Laftah.

Can Sensitive Skin Types Use Actives Around the Eyes?

"Yes," says Dr Laftah, "But it is important to choose gentle, well-formulated products specifically designed for this delicate area. Ingredients such as low-strength retinol or vitamin C may be tolerated by some individuals, but should be introduced gradually to minimise the risk of dryness, redness and irritation." As always, avoid applying actives to already irritated or inflamed skin, and discontinue use if persistent irritation occurs.

Without further ado, shop some of my and Dr Laftah's favourite eye creams for sensitive eyes.

Atoderm Intensive 3-In-1 Eye Care

  • Contains no active ingredients to target pigmentation or dark circles

Why we love it: If you want something ultra-soothing and gentle, Bioderma's eye cream is even safe for newborns. This is a fantastic all-rounder for anyone with very sensitive, dry or eczema-prone skin around the eyes. It's a three-in-one formula that not only hydrates, but also soothes irritation and helps repair the skin barrier.

I was particularly impressed by its patented ingredients, which include a complex that helps limit the adhesion of bacteria that can aggravate dryness. It also contains hyaluronic acid to maintain hydration and plumpness for up to 24 hours. Crucially, it's fragrance-free, ophthalmologically tested, and suitable for contact lens wearers—in fact, it's so gentle it's safe for babies from birth. item.title: I Rarely Shop the Black Friday Sales—These Impossibly Chic, Rich-Looking Trousers Changed My Mind
item.dc:content:
If there was ever a time to finally sort through your wish list, it’s during the Black Friday sales. The annual shopping event has arrived, marking the moment that I finally look at all the pieces I’ve been saving for months and suss out if any are making their way into my basket. As luck would have it, Reformation’s cult Olina trousers that have been on my mind for months are now 25% off.

Reformation has delivered so many cult items, from their beloved Clara cardigan to the viral Jonie scoop neck jumper, that it takes little effort to convince me of their worth. So when this silk taffeta-inspired silhouette arrived on the scene over the summer, I was instantly enamoured with their unique fabric composition and saccharine colour palette.

Though besotted with them from first glance, I was slightly dubious about checking out my basket. Launching in the summer months, I’d seen so many stylish people wearing their own pairs with simple tank tops and relaxed Tees, but I hadn’t quite decided if these trousers would work for my wardrobe all year round. Recently, I spotted style setters pairing their own pairs with soft knits, fluffy jackets and proving that these trousers can move seamlessly from day to night. Now, I’m glad I waited.

Their appeal lies in their uniqueness; compared to stiff denim or slouchy wool, these trousers boast a polished shape that elevates any knit or jacket you pair them with. And as we head into the depths of winter, the ability to make me feel more put-together without any effort is invaluable.

After finally purchasing them, I can safely say that they were well worth the wait. For cosy pub lunches, I pair them with an oversized trench coat and a sumptuous cashmere. For days working from home, they’re the perfect accompaniment to my snug slippers and graphic T-shirts. For nicer outings, I have no trouble dressing them up with a pair of ballet pumps and a minimal blouse.

Still, with so many events on the horizon, I know I’ll also find ways of incorporating them into my party season wardrobe, styling them with slingback heels and a long, theatrical coat. If this isn’t enough of a testimony to convince you of them, I don’t know what is. But if you’re still curious to see what the fuss is about, keep scrolling through to shop the style, along with other Reformation best-sellers, for yourself. That extra £50 back in your pocket is just a bonus.

Shop the Reformation Olina Pants in the 2026 Black Friday Sale
Reformation
Olina Cropped Pant

The navy is a true timeless shade, yet it will add a softer edge to ensembles compared to black counterparts.

Reformation
Olina Cropped Pant

Chartreuse is the shade of the season; piquant, refreshing and a little divisive, it'll add an edge to your winter warmers.

Reformation
Olina Cropped Pant

From knitwear to trousers, royal purple is cropping up in all the right places, including in this seasonal shade.

Reformation
Olina Cropped Pant

Have you seen a more perfect party outfit? From the gold accents to the feather accessories and velvet jacket, the Olina pants just tie it all together.

Reformation
Olina Cropped Pant

With the sun setting in the mid-afternoon, I'm looking to my wardrobe to give me the serotonin boost I would've otherwise sought elsewhere. The glossy sheen on this colourway is the uplift I need.

Reformation
Olina Cropped Pant

Pewter, steel or heather grey; whatever you want to call it, there's no denying how chic it is.

Reformation
Olina Cropped Pant

Brocade and jacquard are two of the most ornate trends you can invest in this season, and this silhouette interprets both in the most subtle, minimal way.

Shop More of Reformation's 2026 Black Friday Sale:

Reformation
Cove Cashmere Oversized Crew

This style boasts a similar shape to The Row's Ophelia jumper, but at a fraction at the price.

Reformation
Jonie Cashmere Oversized Scoop Neck

Though only launched a few months ago, this style has already become a best-seller for the brand. Endorsed by Olivia Jade, it's available in countless colours including this pastel pink.
Reformation
Clara Cashmere Crew Cardigan

Cardigans don't get much more sought after than the Reformation Clara.

Reformation
Stella Coat

Opera coats are swiftly becoming this season's must-have style.

Reformation
Vida Low Rise Pant

Another pair of party pants to add to your rotation.

Reformation
Blair High Rise Baby Bootcut Jeans

Bootcut jeans will dominate through January.

Reformation
Inez Heeled Mule

Beloved by Hailey Bieber, the Inez is a pump that can elevate any outfit.
item.description: Reformation’s Black Friday edit is ridiculously good.
item.dc:creator: Ava Gilchrist
item.dc:description: <p>Ava Gilchrist is the Fashion Writer at Who What Wear UK. Born in Sydney but now based in London, Ava has worked at some of the most prestigious women’s luxury and lifestyle publications, including ELLE, Marie Claire and most recently GRAZIA, where she held the title of Senior Fashion Features Writer. Ava has five years of industry experience, beginning her writing career after graduating with a Bachelor of Communication from the University of Technology, Sydney. Her words fuse style with substance, bringing readers insightful commentary on the latest fashion trends, runway shows, celebrity red carpet offerings, must-have shopping pieces, beauty hacks and pop culture moments. As an editor, Ava has interviewed everyone from Kendall Jenner, Margot Robbie, Zendaya, Emma Corrin, Kylie Minogue and Charli XCX.</p>

item.title: Don’t Put Your Trench Away—These 6 Winter Outfits Are a Testament to How Chic It Still Is
item.dc:content:
Though we’re well into the season of warm wool coats and voluminous puffers, there is plenty of opportunity left to wear trench coats. This classic is typically categorised as a spring and autumn staple, but I find that slightly unfair. With the right layers and outfit components, you can still wear your beloved trench long into the depths of winter. It's more than just a transitional piece; it's a versatile layer that integrates seamlessly into your winter capsule wardrobe, too. It's just about becoming a little more strategic with how you wear it.

When you're sourcing classic winter pieces, a trench may not be top of mind. Yet its iconic silhouette and long-running history are reason enough to keep it within your rotation. With roomier sleeves and a woven construction, it's one of the easiest outerwear pieces to wear over plush wool jumpers or several layers of knits. And because it's lighter, you won't feel nearly as overwhelmed by layers as you do when you're wrapped in a multitude of shirts and jumpers, plus a heavy down coat on top. That said, there are also trench coats that lend themselves to winter aesthetics. Leather, suede and silk finishes all meld together nicely with your other winter staples, from embellished trousers to extra-long scarves.

So if you're looking for an alternative to your black coats and classic winter outerwear choices, the answer is already likely in front of you. But what does a winter trench coat outfit entail exactly? It's a layer or two on top or beneath that takes it from autumnal to winterised; for instance, a cashmere scarf tied over top or a knit you can wear underneath are essential. Then a considered ensemble underneath. When you arrive at wherever you're going and take off your trench cocoon, it's always nice to feel confident about what's underneath. Monochrome outfits, sleek loafers and ballet flats and knitwear layers are all what the most fashionable people reach for when they're styling a trench into their winter rotation.

It's proof that thinking outside the box always garners the best results and shows that clothes often transcend seasonality. For more inspiration, scroll on for six winter outfit ideas featuring trench coats.

6 Chic Trench-Coat Outfits to Try This Winter

1. Silk Trench + Jeans + Printed Trainers

Style Notes: The sheen of a silk trench always brings a luxurious element to your outfit, whether you choose a loose and fluid style or a more structured version. With a matching turtleneck and jeans, you have the foundation of an outfit you can wear all winter—just vary your accessories. Consider statement trainers, animal-print handbags, long earrings or combinations of scarves and hats to personalise it. A shinier trench coat also looks nice with party-ready attire, such as dresses and tailoring.

Shop the Look:

2. Leather Trench + Scarf + Boots

Style Notes: One of the most fashion-forward ways to warm up a trench coat outfit for winter is by adding a scarf over top, which brings in extra colour and texture, too. If you're also finding your usual gabardine trench isn't the right layer, a leather trench is a thicker alternative. Pair your trench with a monochrome, all-black look underneath, including boots in the same shade. This gives a standout base for the scarf and trench.

Shop the Look:
TOTEME
Belted Leather Coat

You can wear your leather trench into spring with jeans.
Taller Marmo
Ming Stole

This scarf will look so elegant draped over or under a trench, but it works with party dresses, too.
KHAITE
Arizona Leather Ankle Boots

If you're after a boot that's sleeker than a Chelsea or platform style, opt for almost-patent leather with a slanted heel.

3. Trench Coat + Wide-Leg Trousers + Gathered Flats

Style Notes: The volume of wide-leg trousers and gathered detailing from shoes like ballet flats or loafers always looks chic underneath a trench coat. It's also helpful to opt for colours that differ from your outerwear so they don't get lost. When actually choosing from your selection of trench coats, the best winter options are those that look unique on their own. This could be a trench coat with a flared hem, an extra-long trench or one with a cape component draped across your back. Coats with these small but interesting details make it easier to feel styled when everything has to be buttoned or belted up.

Shop the Look:
Róhe
Classic Trench

You can wear the collar down or high as a funnel-neck.
COS
Relaxed Wool-Blend Twill Wide-Leg Trousers

This pair will become a staple of your winter capsule wardrobe thanks to the wool blend.
Sézane
Irina Low Ballet Flats

Gathered stitching gives classic ballet flats a more modern look.

4. Trench Coat + Jumper + Loafers

Style Notes: Winter is the season when the art of layering becomes even more important. Through the right layers, you get functionality and comfort, but you also signal your sense of style. You're not beholden to a specific method of layering either—for instance, you can tie an extra knit around your waist for warmth and to play with proportions or wear two jumpers in contrasting colours to pop out from a beige trench. A scarf can go underneath your trench, but can also be draped or tied over the top like a triangle. There are many creative options for creating layered outfits with trenches in the winter; you just have to find what suits you.

Shop the Look:
Sézane
Jonas Coat

White jeans pair so well with both classic and printed trench coats.
COS
Rounded Pure Cashmere Crew-Neck Jumper

Perfect for wearing as is or tying around your waist or shoulders.
MANGO
Leather Penny Loafers

5. Suede Trench + Tailored Trousers + Heels

Style Notes: Like a leather trench, a suede trench coat can give you a thicker layer than others. Its velvet, tactile finish also gives a softened and textured look to your outfits—more so than your average puffer or technical jacket. When your coat is already contributing this much to your outfit, you can lean toward minimalism with the rest. Black tailored trousers and a simple button-down or cashmere jumper are an excellent duo. Oh, and a polished hat really completes the look.

Shop the Look:
Massimo Dutti
Long Suede Trench Coat

A rich beige is such a flexible shade and fits neatly in an autumn, winter or spring wardrobe.
Reformation
Mason Pant Es

The Mason Pant is a long-standing editor and fashion-person favourite when it comes to top-tier tailored trousers.
THE ROW
Lia 55 Suede Pumps

This pair from The Row is still in stock in nearly every size. The angled micro heel is so chic.

6. Trench Coat + Scarf + Ballet Flats

Style Notes: As previously mentioned, a scarf can bring so much. For a fashion-set-approved outfit, drape a long black scarf over your trench and pair it with a matching knit, trousers and ballet flats. Together, it's proof of just how effective simplicity can be. You can always add extra colour or visual dimension through a print scarf or boldly coloured shoes if you'd like, but either way it's a solid winter outfit featuring a trench coat.

Shop the Look:
ALIGNE
Giselle Trench Coat

This trench comes with a detachable faux-fur collar for more styling variations.
NOUR HAMMOUR
Cashmere Scarf

Cashmere looks so polished and will keep you warm all winter.
Massimo Dutti
Soft Leather Ballerinas

The high vamp is a fashionable touch.
item.description: A hero in every sense of the word.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Epifano
item.dc:description: <p>Melissa Epifano Varley is a writer and editor who covers fashion, home, and beauty. She has over seven years of experience and has written for Forbes, InStyle, People, The Zoe Report, and Byrdie. She has also served as the editor-in-chief of Real Homes and lifestyle editor at The Spruce and ran her own wide-fit footwear line for over three years. She graduated a year early from the University of Oregon with a Bachelor of Science in journalism. Melissa has won the PPA Next Gen Award and currently covers fashion, trend, and shopping content for Who What Wear. She’s passionate about helping readers discover their own sense of style in their wardrobes and homes—whether that’s through products, trends, or concepts that they deeply resonate with and makes them feel their best. She’s originally from the U.S. but is now based in Bath where she spends her free time reading books, creatively writing, and taking part in more esoteric endeavours like reiki and tarot.</p>

item.title: I Only Buy Cashmere When It’s on Sale—These Are the 7 Chicest Finds This Black Friday
item.dc:content:
As soon as the temperatures drop for winter, I reassemble my wardrobe with cashmere front and centre. From soft knitwear to cosy accessories, this insulating material features heavily in my daily outfits, leaving many of my friends to wonder how I can afford to have so many sleek cashmere pieces in my rotation. The answer is that I only shop for cashmere when it's on sale, and with plenty of practice, this Black Friday I've rounded up the very best cashmere deals.

As we know, certain materials call for higher price points, and luxurious cashmere is one of them. With a smaller supply than other yarns, this intrinsically cosy fabric can often cost more than other affordable knitwear, but if you want to invest (and know how to shop the sales), cashmere buys can be some of your most worthwhile investments. Last Black Friday, I snapped up a sumptuously soft jumper from Soft Goat which always induces compliments when I wear it, and the year before I added Reformation's Clara cardigan to my collection. Still, years on, it's one of my most relied-upon knits.

In any winter capsule wardrobe, you're sure to find knitwear featuring heavily, and this Black Friday you can add a touch of luxury to your wardrobe with one of the soft cashmere knits below. Alongside, I've hunted for deals on cashmere trousers that will make lounging that much more luxurious this season, as well as a series of sleek cashmere coats that you'll turn to every time the temperature drops.

Finally, you'll find the classic cashmere accessories like scarves and gloves, along with sumptuous cashmere socks, which are a serious game-changer. The best part is that you can also tick off your Christmas gifting list, as cashmere is always a welcome present, and you know they'll appreciate a cosy addition. What Is Black Friday?

Black Friday is an annual shopping event when brands and retailers offer discounts across fashion, beauty, homeware, technology and more. Originating in the United States, it takes place the day after Thanksgiving and has become one of the biggest shopping events of the year in the UK. Today, Black Friday sales often begin weeks before the official date, allowing shoppers to find deals on everything from wardrobe staples to Christmas gifts.

When Is Black Friday 2026?

Black Friday 2026 falls on Friday, 27 November. However, many brands launch their Black Friday sales in the weeks leading up to the date, with some offers available throughout November. The Black Friday shopping period typically continues over the weekend and into Cyber Monday on Monday, 30 November.

When Do Black Friday Sales Start in 2026?

Black Friday sales in 2026 are expected to begin at different times depending on the brand or retailer. Whilst Black Friday itself takes place on Friday, 27 November, many brands launch early offers in the weeks beforehand. Check back regularly for the latest Black Friday deals from your favourite fashion and beauty retailers.

When Do Black Friday Sales End in 2026?

There is no official end date for Black Friday sales. Many retailers extend their offers throughout the Black Friday weekend and into Cyber Monday on Monday, 30 November 2026, whilst others may end their promotions earlier or continue discounting into December. Always check individual retailers for confirmed sale dates and terms.

Which Brands Are Taking Part in Black Friday 2026?

From designer handbags to jewellery and beauty favourites, plenty of brands are offering discounts for Black Friday 2026. This year, you can shop deals from brands including DeMellier, Missoma, Dyson and Elemis, with offers across selected styles and collections. We might even have a few exclusive discounts up our sleeves for you, too! We've rounded up the sales worth knowing about to help you find the best fashion and beauty deals.

What Should I Buy During the Black Friday Sales?

Black Friday is a good opportunity to invest in fashion and beauty pieces you've had your eye on, replenish everyday essentials or get ahead with Christmas shopping. Look out for discounts on winter coats, boots, cashmere, bags, skincare, makeup and fragrance. Before buying, compare prices and check the terms of each offer to make sure you're getting a worthwhile deal.

Are Black Friday Deals Worth It?

Black Friday can be a useful time to shop for fashion and beauty at reduced prices, but not every offer represents the best value. If there's a particular item you've been considering, check its price before the sale begins and compare offers across retailers. Shopping with a wish list in mind can also help you prioritise pieces you'll genuinely wear or use. Our recommendations are selected by our editors who weigh up all the options for you, so you can trust their selections are, in their opinion, worth it.

item.author: florriealexander505@gmail.com (Florrie Alexander)
item.dc:creator: Florrie Alexander
item.dc:description: <p>Florrie embarked on her fashion journey while studying French and History at university. Whilst studying in Aix-en-Provence, she began to write her dissertation on the history of fashion and the influence of Haute Couture, and landed her first role at Harper’s Bazaar. Following this, she interned for various publications including Elle, Grazia and Marie Claire before joining the fashion team at Conde Nast Traveller. There, she contributed to international photoshoots, styled pages and covers, and produced engaging digital content.</p><p>During a freelance period, Florrie honed her skills in editorial work in various digital and print publications, as well as styling e-commerce photoshoots and personal shopping. Whilst acting as a personal shopper, Florrie shopped for clients and styled complete outfits, a skill she brings to outfit ideas and styling guides at Who What Wear UK. Florrie actively pursues an in-depth understanding of fashion and jewellery, and after styling a jewellery cover shoot at Conde Nast Traveller, chose to complete the De Beers Diamond Foundation course. She has a particular love for handbags and a collection to match.</p><p>Florrie first joined Who What Wear UK as a freelancer before becoming the Commerce Writer, blending both editorial and commercial content. Now, as the Shopping Editor, she monitors current trends, new-in styles, wardrobe heroes and how best to style them. In her downtime, Florrie can be found in her hometown of London, usually with a coffee in hand.</p>

What Is Black Friday?

Black Friday is an annual shopping event when brands and retailers offer discounts across fashion, beauty, homeware, technology and more. Originating in the United States, it takes place the day after Thanksgiving and has become one of the biggest shopping events of the year in the UK. Today, Black Friday sales often begin weeks before the official date, allowing shoppers to find deals on everything from wardrobe staples to Christmas gifts.

When Is Black Friday 2026?

Black Friday 2026 falls on Friday, 27 November. However, many brands launch their Black Friday sales in the weeks leading up to the date, with some offers available throughout November. The Black Friday shopping period typically continues over the weekend and into Cyber Monday on Monday, 30 November.

When Do Black Friday Sales Start in 2026?

Black Friday sales in 2026 are expected to begin at different times depending on the brand or retailer. Whilst Black Friday itself takes place on Friday, 27 November, many brands launch early offers in the weeks beforehand. Check back regularly for the latest Black Friday deals from your favourite fashion and beauty retailers.

When Do Black Friday Sales End in 2026?

There is no official end date for Black Friday sales. Many retailers extend their offers throughout the Black Friday weekend and into Cyber Monday on Monday, 30 November 2026, whilst others may end their promotions earlier or continue discounting into December. Always check individual retailers for confirmed sale dates and terms.

Which Brands Are Taking Part in Black Friday 2026?

From designer handbags to jewellery and beauty favourites, plenty of brands are offering discounts for Black Friday 2026. This year, you can shop deals from brands including DeMellier, Missoma, Dyson and Elemis, with offers across selected styles and collections. We might even have a few exclusive discounts up our sleeves for you, too! We've rounded up the sales worth knowing about to help you find the best fashion and beauty deals.

What Should I Buy During the Black Friday Sales?

Black Friday is a good opportunity to invest in fashion and beauty pieces you've had your eye on, replenish everyday essentials or get ahead with Christmas shopping. Look out for discounts on winter coats, boots, cashmere, bags, skincare, makeup and fragrance. Before buying, compare prices and check the terms of each offer to make sure you're getting a worthwhile deal.

Are Black Friday Deals Worth It?

Black Friday can be a useful time to shop for fashion and beauty at reduced prices, but not every offer represents the best value. If there's a particular item you've been considering, check its price before the sale begins and compare offers across retailers. Shopping with a wish list in mind can also help you prioritise pieces you'll genuinely wear or use. Our recommendations are selected by our editors who weigh up all the options for you, so you can trust their selections are, in their opinion, worth it.

item.title: I Set Myself a Strict Black Friday Budget—These 15 Chic Winter Buys Made the Cut
item.dc:content:
When Black Friday rolls around and all my favourite brands suddenly reduce their prices, I have a tendency to get a little carried away. Before I know it, I'm adding things to my basket that I definitely don't need and, quite frankly, wouldn't have given a second glance at full price. A classic Black Friday mistake, and one I'm determined not to repeat this year. Instead, I'm taking a more considered approach, setting myself a strict budget and focusing on the pieces my wardrobe is actually missing. After all, there's no better time to give your winter wardrobe a refresh than when some of the best brands are offering serious discounts.

So, what's on my wish list? First, a great pair of straight-leg jeans that I can wear on repeat with cashmere jumpers, loafers and ankle boots. Next, a beautifully tailored wool coat that will keep me warm without compromising on style. I'm also in desperate need of a jewellery refresh, so a pair of everyday gold hoops and a delicate bracelet have made the cut. And finally, a perfectly tailored pair of trousers that will work just as well for the office as they do for dinner.

The aim isn't to buy an entirely new wardrobe, but to invest in a handful of hardworking pieces that can be mixed, matched and worn for seasons to come. From Mango and Nobody's Child to Reformation and Abercrombie & Fitch, I've scoured the Black Friday sales to put together a capsule wardrobe that feels polished, practical and, most importantly, affordable.

Keep scrolling to shop my ultimate budget-friendly Black Friday capsule wardrobe edit.

Shop My Black Friday Wish List:
Reformation
Clara Cashmere Crew Cardigan

A classic cashmere cardigan is one of those wardrobe staples you'll never regret investing in, and Reformation's Clara is about as good as it gets.
Abercrombie
High Rise 90s Relaxed Jean

Abercrombie makes some of my favourite high-street denim, and this relaxed '90s silhouette is a particularly good example.

Monica Vinader
Gold Vermeil MV Siren Muse Mini Huggie Earrings

A pair of understated gold earrings is always worth having in your jewellery collection.
MANGO
Handmade Oversized Wool Coat

A beautifully cut wool coat can transform even the simplest outfit.

Abercrombie
Bobble-Stitch Crew Cardigan

I love the slightly cropped, fitted silhouette of this cardigan.
Reformation
Cove Cashmere Oversized Crew

A relaxed cashmere jumper is one of the hardest-working pieces in any winter wardrobe.
Nobodys Child
Brown Wool-Blend Funnel Neck Coat

Funnel-neck coats are one of winter's most elegant outerwear trends.
Abercrombie
Gemma Satin Wide Leg Pull-On Pant

Satin trousers are one of my favourite alternatives to jeans for evenings out.
Rise & Fall
Women's Finest Cashmere Wide-Leg Trousers

Cashmere trousers are the ultimate luxury for cosy winter dressing.

Reformation
Jonie Cashmere Oversized Scoop Neck

Between the relaxed fit and elegant neckline, this cashmere jumper has all the makings of a forever favourite.
Nobodys Child
Khaki Whipstitch Asymmetric Wool-Blend Jacket

The contrasting whipstitch detailing gives this jacket a distinctly elevated feel.
Levi Strauss & Co.
Ribcage Full Length Jeans

If you prefer a more defined waist, Levi's Ribcage jeans are well worth considering.
Missoma
Tennis Everyday Bracelet | Missoma Uk

A delicate tennis bracelet is one of those jewellery pieces that never goes out of style.

MANGO
Long Bambi Faux-Fur Coat

The perfect statement coat. Keep the rest of the outfit understated with black trousers and sleek boots.
Whistles
Dark Denim Authentic Barrel Leg Jean

The perfect dark wash barrel-leg jeans.
Missoma
Savi Dome Mini Hoop Earrings - 18ct Gold Plated

A great pair of gold hoops for every day.
Whistles
Neutral Bold Shoulder Crew Neck Knit

Pair with dark-wash jeans and a chocolate brown suede bag.
Reformation
Olina Cropped Pant

These relaxed, cropped trousers are a chic alternative to traditional tailoring.
RIXO
Joann - Bohemia Leopard

Leopard print has earned its place as a modern neutral, and this statement coat is proof.

Whistles
Black Heeled Leather Knee High Boot

These sleek leather boots are the kind you'll reach for all winter.
Whistles
Black Noelle Suede Buckle Tote Bag

Such an expensive-looking find.
item.dc:creator: Marina Avraam
item.dc:description: <p>Marina Avraam is Senior Shopping Editor at <em>Who What Wear UK</em>, where she expertly navigates Zara, H&M, Toteme and Net-a-Porter (to name but a few) on a daily basis to unearth the most worthwhile pieces, while valiantly resisting the urge to add every single one to her basket. With 6 years of experience in the fashion industry, prior to joining <em>Who What Wear</em>, Marina was Deputy Commerce Editor at <em>Grazia UK</em>, where she honed her trend-spotting skills and ability to predict exactly what audiences want to shop and when. At <em>Who What Wear</em>, Marina is committed to curating a shopping experience that feels both aspirational and intentional, guiding readers to items—both affordable and investment—that will genuinely benefit their wardrobes. </p>
