item.title: My Aunt Is Shopping for Jeans, Coats, and Sweaters—Here Are the Nordstrom Cyber Week Deals I Sent Her
item.dc:content:
Nordstrom's Cyber Week sale has started, and it's up to 60% off. With Nordstrom being one of our readers' favorite places to shop, we've been covering the sale from all angles—with even more to come as the week goes on. So far, Jennifer Camp Forbes has covered the top trends from the sale: fur-trimmed coats and jackets, ballet pumps, relaxed jeans, cropped trench coats, and woven bags; Chichi Offor has curated the best sneaker deals; and Bobby Schuessler has predicted what items he thinks could sell out.

My aunt is currently shopping for jeans, coats, and sweaters, so I went through the sale to see what I could find to send her. For jeans, Levi's is the standout, with the best-selling 501 '90s pair on sale for 33% off at $74. Pistola and Mother also have ones marked down.

In the coats section, I have a feeling she'll like Madewell's The Simone Cocoon Coat and Eileen Fisher's Wing Collar Tie Waist Wool Coat, as well as the faux-fur options. There are so many on-sale sweaters as well, from brands like Reformation, Mango, and Nordstrom's own in-house cashmere line. Ahead, shop these and more of the best jean, coat, and sweater discounts at Nordstrom for Black Friday.

item.title: Dylan Efron on Marathon Training, His Unconventional "8-Mile" Philosophy, and Post-Run Skincare Staples
item.dc:content:
Dylan Efron ran the New York City Marathon in three hours and 28 minutes. That’s an average pace of 7:52 per mile—impressive for seasoned marathoners, let alone trainees and first-timers. A background in endurance sports certainly helps. He’s completed multiple marathons, various triathlons, and even full Ironmans (once ranked in the top 1% of his age group). Off-duty, he stays active, sharing his love for rock climbing, cycling, surfing, and the like.

Efron is a true athlete, but that doesn’t mean he doesn’t accept help where he can find it. On race days, he takes advantage of every aid station along a 26.2-mile route (even if it’s just to pour a cup of cool water over his head). He opens an energy gel every 30 minutes. And after he crosses the finish line, he turns to a one-and-done serum to help his skin recover from sun and wind. Ahead, read WWW’s exclusive interview with Efron, in which he talks about skincare, his unconventional eight-mile training philosophy, race-day recovery, and more.
Olay
Super Serum

Efron partnered with Olay ahead of the NYC Marathon to promote the brand’s Super Serum, a 5-in-1 formula that hydrates, smoothes, firms, brightens, and evens the skin. While it would be easy to write off another celebrity skincare endorsement, it’s obvious that Efron is 1) genuinely excited about the product, and 2) actually uses it as part of his crowded work and training schedule. "In general, the things I'm passionate about are really easy for me to talk about, and [skincare] is my new little passion," he says. "Olay is a brand I've known forever. It's tried and trusted for me. I grew up with it."

While he admits that the world of skincare (and yes, it’s a whole world) is somewhat new to him, he’s happily exploring it with help from the iconic drugstore brand. "Some of the people I follow have much more involved routines. It's vitamin C, oil, collagen, peptides, and all these other things. I live out of a suitcase half the time, so with the Olay Super Serum, I'm getting five of those ingredients right out of the gate."

His first foray into skincare was via eye patches—a true gateway product. "It started with eye patches, and now I can't go a morning without them," he laughs. "It's like coffee for my eyes. I wake up and put them on." Even though he uses them almost every morning, he has yet to find a favorite set. In fact, it’s clear the question strikes a skincare chord—the man has opinions. "I've done a lot of experimenting with them. I was even joking that I want to start my own because I like certain things about different brands. I like the ones that come in a circular case with a bunch of patches because they're great for everyday use and you're not wasting plastic. However, the shape of them is terrible. They're too wide in some places and too narrow in others. I also like the ones that have hyaluronic acid. I feel like there's a combination of things I'm looking for: the right shape, good ingredients, and individual packaging."

Olay
Super Cream Face Moisturizer With SPF 30

Beyond eye patches, Efron is down to experiment in other areas of his skincare routine. His previous bare-bones routine consisted of moisturizer and lip balm. Now, though, he’s venturing into things like vitamin C and retinol. “I vividly remember when I was trying a new moisturizer with vitamin C. I didn't think much of it, but I got about five comments on how good my skin looked. I was like, ‘All right, this stuff works.’ Now I'm fully invested.”

Since then, he’s expanded his routine to add some heavyweight active ingredients. “AHAs and retinol are the two ingredients I'm newest to. They can make your skin more vulnerable to the sun. When I use those ingredients, I have to switch into science mode and remind myself, ‘All right, I'm putting this on, so make sure to put on SPF in the morning."

Still, he sticks to the Super Serum for his AM skincare routine. “With the amount of running I've been doing, I use it right after I go for a run and shower. It helps my skin bounce back,” he says. “I put it on before moisturizer and sunscreen. I have a bunch of different tinted sunscreens I like. The good thing about the moisturizer I pair with it, the Olay Super Cream Moisturizer, is that it already has SPF 30 in it. Then I do add additional tinted sunscreen on top of that.”

Efron says his new passion for skincare was born partly out of necessity, as endurance training is as tough on the skin as it is on the body. “I think it's the sun exposure, the double showering, and the sweat,” he says. “It really beats your skin up. I remember when I was biking a lot, my eyes were getting messed up because of the sun exposure. My cornea was actually getting burned because I wasn't wearing sunglasses.” The same goes for running. “Running means spending a lot of time outside and getting a lot of sun exposure. It really dries out your skin and sucks the life out of it,” he says.

His training schedule, though not as time-consuming as it used to be, is still impressive. “About 10 years ago, I was ranked in the top one percent of my age group for Ironman,” he says. “Life has changed a lot in the last 10 years, though, and I don't have the time I used to have to train.” These days, he swears by an unconventional marathon-training philosophy. “I like this theory of no long runs. I see everybody doing these 20-mile runs, but personally, I don't get anything out of that. It takes me a week to bounce back, and my Achilles gets a little sore. I don't think 20-mile runs are good for you, and I'd rather save that effort for the marathon itself.”

He theorizes that he gets the most benefit out of speed training: “Running fast is the best way to get a good marathon time,” he says. That’s why, believe it or not, he caps his longest run at eight miles. He admits it’s an “ambitious” training philosophy, but he’s sticking to it. “You just have to grit it out. A 20-mile run isn't necessarily going to prepare you for that. No matter what, you just have to grit it out on race day.”

Having run so many races already, Efron is an obvious source of expertise for first-time runners. His advice ranges from the practical to the profound. “The day before, I really like compression socks for a marathon. Anything that helps keep the blood flowing in your legs is great. I also like my Therabody massage gun to keep my muscles loose, along with foam rolling. That's probably my biggest thing. The night before a marathon, I'm going to be stretching and foam rolling all night.” Outside of that, it comes down to mental preparation (and bathroom strategy). “Your body knows what it's about to do, and you have to trust that it's going to prepare itself. I think you should wake up early, let your body get ready, and don't panic or miss your chance to use the bathroom because you've heard the horror stories,” he laughs.

During the race, Efron says it’s important to manage energy. “During that first hour, I'll try to have some type of bar, like a Bobo's bar or something that's high in carbs and easy to get down. Then, I take a gel every 30 minutes. Toward the end of the race, I'll start taking ones with caffeine. I think that really helps give me the energy to finish.”

Most of all, though, Efron tells first-time marathoners to take advantage of every aid station along the route. “When I pass an aid station, something I learned during my triathlon days is to grab the first cup of water and dump it on my head. Your body is emanating heat, and your heart rate is going up. I'll take that cold water, dump it on my head, and immediately feel a boost of relief. Then I'll drink the water, followed by Gatorade. I'm taking full advantage of every water station to hydrate and get in my supplements. I think that's key in a race that long.”
Science in Sport
Beta Fuel + Nootropics Energy Gel, Lemon & Lime

After the race, it’s all about recovery, both for the body and skin. “Going back to my eight-mile theory, I think that's where I pay for it,” he says. “ I think the people who are putting in 100-mile weeks and really training hard won't be as banged up as me.” After “limping” back home, Efron showers and puts his legs up against the wall. “A lot of people use high-compression pants, which I love, but the easiest hack is to lie with your butt against the corner of the room and your legs up the wall. I think that has always helped me after a race, just to get the blood flowing back out of my legs.”

Last but not least, he applies the Super Serum to revitalize his skin after hours of environmental pollution, sweat, and exertion. It might not be the most obvious marathon recovery step, but he says it’s worth it. “I think as long as someone is open to learning and willing to try something, they're going to see the benefits. Being open to something a little untraditional is good in life.”

It helps my skin bounce back,” he says. “I put it on before moisturizer and sunscreen. I have a bunch of different tinted sunscreens I like. The good thing about the moisturizer I pair with it, the Olay Super Cream Moisturizer, is that it already has SPF 30 in it. Then I do add additional tinted sunscreen on top of that.”

Efron says his new passion for skincare was born partly out of necessity, as endurance training is as tough on the skin as it is on the body. “I think it's the sun exposure, the double showering, and the sweat,” he says. “It really beats your skin up. I remember when I was biking a lot, my eyes were getting messed up because of the sun exposure. My cornea was actually getting burned because I wasn't wearing sunglasses.” The same goes for running. “Running means spending a lot of time outside and getting a lot of sun exposure. It really dries out your skin and sucks the life out of it,” he says.

His training schedule, though not as time-consuming as it used to be, is still impressive. “About 10 years ago, I was ranked in the top one percent of my age group for Ironman,” he says. “Life has changed a lot in the last 10 years, though, and I don't have the time I used to have to train.” These days, he swears by an unconventional marathon-training philosophy. “I like this theory of no long runs. I see everybody doing these 20-mile runs, but personally, I don't get anything out of that. It takes me a week to bounce back, and my Achilles gets a little sore. I don't think 20-mile runs are good for you, and I'd rather save that effort for the marathon itself.”

He theorizes that he gets the most benefit out of speed training: “Running fast is the best way to get a good marathon time,” he says. That’s why, believe it or not, he caps his longest run at eight miles. He admits it’s an “ambitious” training philosophy, but he’s sticking to it. “You just have to grit it out. A 20-mile run isn't necessarily going to prepare you for that. No matter what, you just have to grit it out on race day.”

Having run so many races already, Efron is an obvious source of expertise for first-time runners. His advice ranges from the practical to the profound. “The day before, I really like compression socks for a marathon. Anything that helps keep the blood flowing in your legs is great. I also like my Therabody massage gun to keep my muscles loose, along with foam rolling. That's probably my biggest thing. The night before a marathon, I'm going to be stretching and foam rolling all night.” Outside of that, it comes down to mental preparation (and bathroom strategy). “Your body knows what it's about to do, and you have to trust that it's going to prepare itself. I think you should wake up early, let your body get ready, and don't panic or miss your chance to use the bathroom because you've heard the horror stories,” he laughs.

During the race, Efron says it’s important to manage energy. “During that first hour, I'll try to have some type of bar, like a Bobo's bar or something that's high in carbs and easy to get down. Then, I take a gel every 30 minutes. Toward the end of the race, I'll start taking ones with caffeine. I think that really helps give me the energy to finish.”

Most of all, though, Efron tells first-time marathoners to take advantage of every aid station along the route. “When I pass an aid station, something I learned during my triathlon days is to grab the first cup of water and dump it on my head. Your body is emanating heat, and your heart rate is going up. I'll take that cold water, dump it on my head, and immediately feel a boost of relief. Then I'll drink the water, followed by Gatorade. I'm taking full advantage of every water station to hydrate and get in my supplements. I think that's key in a race that long.”
Science in Sport
Beta Fuel + Nootropics Energy Gel, Lemon & Lime

After the race, it’s all about recovery, both for the body and skin. “Going back to my eight-mile theory, I think that's where I pay for it,” he says. “ I think the people who are putting in 100-mile weeks and really training hard won't be as banged up as me.” After “limping” back home, Efron showers and puts his legs up against the wall. “A lot of people use high-compression pants, which I love, but the easiest hack is to lie with your butt against the corner of the room and your legs up the wall. I think that has always helped me after a race, just to get the blood flowing back out of my legs.”

Last but not least, he applies the Super Serum to revitalize his skin after hours of environmental pollution, sweat, and exertion. It might not be the most obvious marathon recovery step, but he says it’s worth it. “I think as long as someone is open to learning and willing to try something, they're going to see the benefits. Being open to something a little untraditional is good in life.”

item.title: These Are Elegant Pants Every It Girl Wears to the Airport
item.dc:content:
There’s an art to dressing for the airport. The look should feel effortless, naturally chic, and, above all, comfortable enough to carry you through a cross-country flight or a red-eye without sacrificing style. While leggings and traditional sweatpants have long been the default for travel days, the fashion set has embraced a more polished alternative: elastic-waist pants. Think fluid silhouettes, elevated draping, impeccable tailoring, and the kind of relaxed elegance that makes even a 6 a.m. departure feel considered. They offer all the ease of your favorite lounge pants, with a decidedly more sophisticated finish.

The secret is in the details. Labels like The Row have perfected the art of effortless dressing with styles such as the Gala pants, where an elasticated waist meets a refined silhouette. Meanwhile, Almada makes a compelling case for crepe pants, proving that comfort and structure can coexist beautifully. Elsewhere, drawstring details, wide-leg cuts, soft tailoring, and elevated satin fabrics are giving the humble pull-on pant a fashion-forward spin. Paired with an oversized cashmere sweater, a crisp white shirt, or a tailored jacket, these are the pieces that look just as good arriving at the terminal as they do stepping out at your destination. Consider them the modern travel uniform: equal parts practical and polished, and proof that looking put-together can be low-key. Ahead, the elegant elastic-waist pants to add to your travel uniform.

item.dc:description: <p>Kristen Nichols is the Associate Director, Special Projects at Who What Wear with over a decade of experience in fashion, editorial, and publishing. She oversees luxury and runway content, and covers fashion within the luxury market, runway reporting, shopping features, trends, and interviews with leading industry experts. She also contributes to podcast recordings, social media, and branded content initiatives. Kristen has worked with brands including Prada, Chanel, Tiffany &amp; Co., and MyTheresa, and her style has been featured in publications including The New York Times, Vogue.com, Vogue France, WWD, and the CFDA. Before Who What Wear, Kristen began her career at Rodarte, where she worked on styling, photo shoots, and runway shows, and at Allure, where she moved into print and digital editorial. She graduated from the University of Southern California, where she studied art history and business, and currently lives in New York.</p>

item.title: The Winter 2026 It-Girl Wardrobe: 7 Highly Specific Brands and Buys They're Wearing
item.dc:content:
Welcome to It-Girl Wardrobes, a quarterly column by Anna LaPlaca that downloads you on the exact brands and items that fashion people are unanimously backing for the current season.

In my corner of the internet, all the coolest people are agreeing on the same few buys. The brand behind the calf-hair, shearling, and fur-trimmed coats they're all wearing this winter? They're Nour Hammour. The one item that all the insiders are buying from The Row right now? None other than the viral tasseled Men's Loafers. The pretty diamond drop earrings that are taking over my feed (and wish list) right now? That would be the Dorsey Sylvie Rivière Earrings. You see, the best dressers I know all seem to gravitate toward the same few items each season, and today, I'm making it my mission to document and outline them all here. Consider this your directory for cool winter 2026 style.

Whether it's a specific denim shape everyone's wearing, cult-loved designer loafers, or a singular accessory that transforms every cold-weather outfit, each of the seven brands and buys below come together to represent what good style looks like right now, at least according to the tastemakers I personally follow and take inspiration from. With that, discover all the highly specific brands and items that the best dressed women are all wearing ahead.

Nour Hammour Outerwear

When it comes to the coolest outerwear pieces of the winter, Parisian label Nour Hammour is always at the scene of the crime. Each year, one or two of its styles breaks through as the season's It coat and right now, it's the Stella Calf Hair Coat that's the most-wanted among fashion insiders.
NOUR HAMMOUR
Stella Paneled Calf Hair Coat
Nour Hammour
Sima Shearling Coat
Nour Hammour
Ravina Shearling Coat
Nour Hammour
Clara Croc-Effect Leather Jacket

Flared Jeans

Slim bootcut jeans were everywhere this fall, but heading into winter I'm starting to notice denim veering into more true flared territory with Elsa Hosk in a pair of R13 Overflow Boy Flares and Bella Hadid wearing the Frame Le Flare Jeans on repeat.
R13
Overflow Boy Flare
FRAME
The Flare High-Rise Jeans
AGOLDE
Low Rise Boot Jeans
EB Denim
Maria Slim Low Rise Bootcut Jeans

Dorsey Sylvie Rivière Earrings

It girls and Dorsey jewelry—it's an ongoing love story at this point. This season, though, the style set has narrowed in on one style in particular: the Sylvie Rivière Drop Earrings. They feature a cascading silhouette of round moissanite stones and look just as chic worn with a plain white tee as they do finishing a cocktail dress.

Dorsey
Short Sylvie Rivière Earrings in Moissanite, Gold Vermeil With White Rhodium Bezel
Dorsey
Short Sylvie Rivière Earrings in Moissanite, Sterling Silver
Dorsey
Short Sylvie Rivière Earrings in Moissanite, Gold Vermeil

The Row Men's Loafers

The Row accessories are always in constant rotation, but right now cool girls are gravitating towards the Men's Loafer, a pair of tassel-finished leather loafers that despite their name are part of the women's assortment. The tassel just lends the shoes such a sophisticated feel.

The Row
Men's Loafer
The Row
Men's Loafer

Carelli Jackets

Fur trimming is the trend of the season, and Carelli is the brand behind some of the coolest and most sought-after styles. The brand focuses on faux-fur and leather jackets, and each piece is a statement-maker but surprisingly easy to wear at the same time—I've noticed the style set's go-to outfit pairing is with denim and flats.

Liffner Pushlock Clutches

Liffner's Pushlock Clutch, that comes in a range of finishes from crushed velvet and animal-printed calf hair to croc embossing, is a particular favorite among fashion people.

Ostrich-Print Accessories

The key to looking expensive this winter? Styling something ostrich-printed. The exotic finish is popping up everywhere and any handbag, belt, or pair of shoes it appears on instantly makes them look so expensive, chic, and forward.

item.dc:creator: Anna LaPlaca
item.dc:description: <p>Anna is an editor on the fashion team at Who What Wear and has been at the company for over eight years, having begun her career in the Los Angeles office before relocating to New York, where she's currently based. Having always been passionate about pursuing a career in fashion, she built up her experience interning at the likes of Michael Kors, A.L.C., and College Fashionista before joining the team as a post-graduate assistant editor. Anna has penned a number of interviews with Who What Wear's cover stars over the years, including A-listers Megan Fox, Issa Rae, and Emma Chamberlain. She's earned a reputation for scouting new and emerging brands from across the globe and championing them to our audience of millions. While fashion is her main wheelhouse, Anna led the launch of WWW Travels last year, a new lifestyle vertical that highlights all things travel through a fashion-person lens. She is passionate about shopping vintage, whether it be at a favorite local outpost or an on-the-road discovery, and has amassed a wardrobe full of unique finds. When she's not writing, you can find her shooting street imagery on her film camera, attempting to learn a fourth or fifth language, or planning her next trip across the globe.</p>

item.title: Black Friday Is the Best Time to Stock Up on Cashmere—Here's Where to Shop
item.dc:content:
With so many Black Friday sales, it can be difficult to know which deals are actually worth it. If there's one thing I suggest to my friends and family, it's cashmere. It's one of those wardrobe investments that never goes out of style, and when you find quality pieces at a good price, that's even better. Enter Naadam, the label editors love for its luxurious cashmere selection. For Black Friday, the brand is offering up to 60% off select styles, making it the perfect opportunity to stock up on everyday knits that are more wallet-friendly.

From classic crewneck sweaters and relaxed cardigans to cozy, cold-weather accessories, Naadam has plenty of elevated essentials you'll instantly add to your winter rotation. Whether you're shopping for yourself or looking for a thoughtful holiday gift, these are the deals you don't want to miss.

Sweaters

You can never have too many good cashmere sweaters. I'm always drawn to classic silhouettes that I can style a million ways for the office, casual weekends, and everything in between. Start with a crewneck or boatneck in a neutral shade, and then venture into a fun color (like pink) if you're looking to switch things up.
NAADAM
Luxe Cashmere Quarter Zip Sweater
NAADAM
Luxe Cashmere Boxy Crewneck Sweater
NAADAM
Luxe Cashmere Oversized Crewneck Sweater
NAADAM
Lightweight Cashmere Boatneck Sweater

Tees & Tanks

While Naadam has mastered its lightweight cashmere tees (I find them super breathable with an effortlessly relaxed fit), I also turn to the brand for its cotton tees and tanks. Take the Lightweight Brushed Cotton Slim Tee, for example. It's pretty much the definition of the perfect white tee: buttery soft, slightly cropped, and made from 100% brushed Pima cotton.
NAADAM
Lightweight Brushed Cotton Slim Tee
NAADAM
Baby Rib Cropped Tank
NAADAM
Lightweight Cashmere Short Sleeve V-Neck Sweater
NAADAM
Super Fine Cashmere T-Shirt

Cardigans

If you ask me, a cashmere cardigan is always worth having on hand. I love the idea of throwing one over a simple tank or wearing it buttoned up with a pair of tailored trousers. It's an easy way to pull an outfit together without having to think too hard about it.
NAADAM
Super Fine Cashmere Classic Cardigan
NAADAM
Signature Cashmere Crewneck Cardigan
NAADAM
Lightweight Cashmere Open Front Cardigan
NAADAM
Lightweight Cashmere Cable Oversized Cardigan

Accessories

Let's be honest: The best part about winter style is all the little layering moments. These beanies, scarves, and socks are even better than your average accessories thanks to Naadam's signature cashmere, which gives each piece an extra-cozy, plush feel. Did I mention they also make excellent gifts?
NAADAM
Signature Cashmere Ribbed Beanie
NAADAM
Super Luxe Cashmere Scarf
NAADAM
Signature Cashmere Ribbed Striped Socks
NAADAM
Signature Cashmere Gloves

item.title: The Luxury Brands and Trends That Shaped Fashion This Year
item.dc:content:
Welcome to The Who What Wear Podcast. Think of it as your direct line to the designers, stylists, beauty experts, editors, and tastemakers who are shaping the fashion-and-beauty world. Subscribe to The Who What Wear Podcast on YouTube, Apple Podcasts, and Spotify.

If you're tired of seeing TikToks on your FYP about "quiet luxury" being the trend you need to add to your wardrobe, you may be in luck.

"I think 'quiet luxury' is one of those phrases we're kind of sick of hearing about, and I think we can finally leave it behind," Who What Wear's Kristen Nichols said of this year's luxury report.

In 2026, the fashion industry ushered in a new era of bold styles, with personality-driven looks at the center.

"This was the year that individuality and personality-driven fashion took center stage through new pieces people were buying, vintage pieces people were sourcing," Nichols said.

In the latest episode of The Who What Wear Podcast, Nichols shares the designers that stood out this year, the emerging designers to watch out for, and more.

To read excerpts from the full interview, scroll below.

Can you tell me some of the biggest shifts you've noticed in the past year in the luxury space?

I think "quiet luxury" is one of those phrases we're kind of sick of hearing about, and I think we can finally leave it behind.

This was the year that individuality and personality-driven fashion took center stage through new pieces people were buying, vintage pieces people were sourcing.

I think we'll see that even more through next year as well.

I also want to hear about key brands that have shaped the landscape this year and why they were successful from your point of view.

I was reflecting on what we were discussing last year, and it was the shift of every designer stepping into a new house, and there were so many, but I think one of the biggest success stories was Matthieu Blazy at Chanel.

What's interesting about what's happening there is he's really just ushering in this new generation of shoppers with all of his print and color and kind of irreverence.

There's a playfulness that I think is very core to Chanel, but we didn't see as much in the past years.

What are the other names you think that are getting their market share of the luxury conversation that are a bit more emerging?

I think, specifically, in New York, we're seeing this new wave of younger designers, which to me is so exciting because I think in the aughts there was a lot of this, and then it kind of died down a little bit.

Now there's really this fresh wave of new talent. One of the most exciting brands in New York right now, I think, is Kallmeyer.

I think she started out maybe a little bit more pared back and minimal, but it's been interesting to see her brand really evolve.

I was at her show in New York this September, and she had just these really beautiful romantic organza fabrics, beaded jackets, and I really just loved the collection.

Conner Ives
Pleated Knit Top
KALLMEYER
Emilee Fringed Skirt in Pique Deco

Then I think a few other names that come to mind, especially coming off of the CFDA Awards are Rachel Scott [of Diotima], who won Womenswear Designer of the Year, and then Colleen Allen, who won Emerging Designer of the Year.

I think that they deserve all the awards. They're so talented. People are so excited about them and what they're doing. All three of these actually are female designers. It's an exciting moment.
Diotima

Colleen Allen

Welcome to The Who What Wear Podcast. Think of it as your direct line to the designers, stylists, beauty experts, editors, and tastemakers who are shaping the fashion-and-beauty world. Subscribe to The Who What Wear Podcast on YouTube, Apple Podcasts, and Spotify.

If you're tired of seeing TikToks on your FYP about "quiet luxury" being the trend you need to add to your wardrobe, you may be in luck.

"I think 'quiet luxury' is one of those phrases we're kind of sick of hearing about, and I think we can finally leave it behind," Who What Wear's Kristen Nichols said of this year's luxury report.

In 2026, the fashion industry ushered in a new era of bold styles, with personality-driven looks at the center.

"This was the year that individuality and personality-driven fashion took center stage through new pieces people were buying, vintage pieces people were sourcing," Nichols said.

In the latest episode of The Who What Wear Podcast, Nichols shares the designers that stood out this year, the emerging designers to watch out for, and more.

To read excerpts from the full interview, scroll below.

This was the year that individuality and personality-driven fashion took center stage through new pieces people were buying, vintage pieces people were sourcing.

I think we'll see that even more through next year as well.

I also want to hear about key brands that have shaped the landscape this year and why they were successful from your point of view.

I was reflecting on what we were discussing last year, and it was the shift of every designer stepping into a new house, and there were so many, but I think one of the biggest success stories was Matthieu Blazy at Chanel.

What's interesting about what's happening there is he's really just ushering in this new generation of shoppers with all of his print and color and kind of irreverence.

There's a playfulness that I think is very core to Chanel, but we didn't see as much in the past years.
